nodes.name: Solvothermal synthesis of Ru1Co precursor
nodes.procedure: 0.08 M CoCl2·6H2O and 0.15 M NaOH were dissolved in 40 ml of 1,4-butanediol to form solution A. 0.015 g RuCl3·xH2O were dissolved in 5 mL of 1,4-butanediol to form solution B. Subsequently, solution B was gradually introduced into solution A under vigorous stirring for 30 min. The mixed solution was then heated to 230°C for 20 min.

unit_operations.name: Mixing
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: solution B was gradually introduced into solution A under vigorous stirring for 30 min.

nodes.name: Post-synthesis processing and hcp-Ru1Co annealing
nodes.procedure: The resulting product was washed with ethanol and acetone several times, and dried under vacuum at 60°C for 3 h. Finally, the precursor powder was annealed at 300°C for 30 min at N2 atmosphere with a heating rate of 5°C min⁻¹ to form hcp-·Ru1Co.

nodes.name: Annealing of hcp/fcc-Ru1Co
nodes.procedure: The precursor powder obtained from solvothermal step was annealed at 500°C for 30 min at N2 atmosphere with a heating rate of 5°C min⁻¹ to form hcp/fcc-·Ru1Co.

nodes.name: Annealing of fcc-Ru1Co
nodes.procedure: The precursor powder obtained from solvothermal step was annealed at 700°C for 30 min at N2 atmosphere with a heating rate of 5°C min⁻¹ to form fcc-·Ru1Co.

nodes.characterization_summary: hcp-Ru1Co shows diffraction peaks matching hcp-Co (JCPDS No. 05-0727) with slight negative shifts; hcp/fcc-Ru1Co shows mixed phases; fcc-Ru1Co matches fcc-Co (JCPDS No. 15-0806).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal phases of synthesized samples are characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD). As shown in Fig. 1b, d, the diffraction peaks of hcp-·Ru1Co match well with those of hcp-Co (JCPDS No. 05-0727), while fcc-·Ru1Co exhibits the diffraction peaks well indexed to fcc-Co (JCPDS No. 15-0806).

nodes.characterization_summary: All Ru1Co SAAs show consistent Co/Ru atomic ratio of 99.25/0.75.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) analysis confirms consistent Co/Ru atomic ratios of 99.25/0.75 in all Ru1Co SAAs (Supplementary Table 1).

nodes.characterization_summary: All three Ru1Co SAAs exhibit homogeneous nanourchin morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of hcp-·Ru1Co is investigated through transmission electron microscopy (TEM) ... TEM image confirms the preserved nano-urchin morphology ... TEM image reveals the conserved nano-urchin structure.

properties.description: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image showing nanostructure with radial, flower-like or starburst morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic dispersion of Ru in Co matrix verified for all three Ru1Co SAAs by HAADF-STEM imaging and 3D surface plot analysis showing isolated bright Ru spots.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic dispersion of Ru in the Co matrix is verified by HAADF-STEM (Fig. 2b) and 3D surface plot analysis (Fig. 2c) ... High-intensity spots represent Ru atoms, while low-intensity spots correspond to Co atoms.

properties.peaks: multiple sharp peaks labeled with Ru and C

nodes.characterization_summary: hcp-Ru1Co shows atomic columns along [110] zone axis matching hcp-Co model with interplanar spacings 0.21 nm (110) and 0.19 nm (111); fcc-Ru1Co shows 0.21 nm (111) for fcc-Co; hcp/fcc shows mixed phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic arrangement of hcp-·Ru1Co is further revealed by high-resolution AC-HAADF-STEM ... Interplanar spacings measured from the intensity profiles ... are 0.21 and 0.19 nm, corresponding to the (110) and (111) planes.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru/Co atomic ratio of 99.24/0.76 in hcp-Ru1Co nano-urchin structure, consistent with ICP-OES.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) reveals the Ru/Co atomic ratio of 99.24/0.76 (Supplementary Fig. 3), consistent with ICP-OES results.

properties.technique: Transmission Electron Microscopy with Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy

nodes.characterization_summary: Metallic Co and Ru dominant; Ru 3p3/2 binding energies: hcp-Ru1Co 461.38 eV, hcp/fcc 461.79 eV, fcc 462.01 eV, indicating reduced electron density on Ru in hcp phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS analysis confirms that metallic Co and Ru are dominant ... The Ru 3p XPS spectrum of hcp-Ru1Co exhibits peaks at 461.38 and 483.56 eV ... positive shift ... for hcp/fcc ·Ru1Co (461.79 eV) and fcc-·Ru1Co (462.01 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge shows metallic characteristics with electron transfer from Co to Ru; hcp-Ru1Co shows strongest electronic interaction; Ru K-edge confirms reduced Ru valence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4a displays the normalized Co K-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra ... the Co K-edge adsorption of hcp-Ru1Co positively shifts compared to fcc ·Ru1Co and hcp/fcc-Ru1Co.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge FT-EXAFS shows Ru-Co bond lengths: hcp-Ru1Co 2.10 Å, hcp/fcc 2.13 Å, fcc 2.17 Å; confirms atomic dispersion (no Ru-Ru bond).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In contrast, hcp-Ru1Co, hcp/fcc-·Ru1Co, and fcc-·Ru1Co exhibit the prominent peaks at 2.10, 2.13, and 2.17 Å, respectively. The significant differences ... suggest that the prominent peak ... is ... Ru–Co metallic bond.

properties.description: Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure plot showing radial distribution

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ CO-DRIFTS of hcp-Ru1Co shows peaks at 2170 and 2121 cm⁻¹ corresponding to mononuclear Ru^δ+(CO) and tricarbonyl Ru^δ+(CO)₃ species, absence of peaks below 2000 cm⁻¹ confirms no Ru clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Following CO adsorption at room temperature, two broad peaks at 2170 and 2121 cm⁻¹ are observed, corresponding to the mononuclear (Ru^δ+(CO)) and tricarbonyl species adsorbed on single Ru atom (Ru^δ+(CO)₃), respectively. The absence of peaks below 2000 cm⁻¹ ... confirms the absence of Ru clusters or nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Surface potentials: hcp-Ru1Co 155 mV, hcp/fcc-Ru1Co 100 mV, fcc-Ru1Co 44 mV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The average surface potential of hcp-·Ru1Co achieved by contact potential difference is 155 mV, substantially exceeding that of hcp/fcc-Ru1Co (100 mV) and fcc-·Ru1Co (44 mV).

nodes.characterization_summary: hcp-Ru1Co shows larger BET surface area consistent with higher ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: hcp-·Ru1Co possesses a larger electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) compared to hcp/fcc-·Ru1Co and fcc-Ru1Co ... consistent with the N2 adsorption–desorption results (Supplementary Fig. 38).

nodes.characterization_summary: N2 adsorption-desorption isotherms used to determine BET surface areas; hcp-Ru1Co shows largest BET surface area consistent with highest ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: hcp-·Ru1Co possesses a larger electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) compared to hcp/fcc-·Ru1Co and fcc-Ru1Co (Supplementary Fig. 37, Table 5), consistent with the N2 adsorption–desorption results (Supplementary Fig. 38).
